signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 currency strength scorecard flags CHF outperforming with a +1.506% 1W average across 6 pairs, while AUD lags at −0.880% across 4 pairs, driving a 2.386% leader-to-laggard spread. AUD/USD trades at 0.6630, below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.6823/0.6934/0.7039 in a sustained downtrend extended 3.96 ATR below its 20-day moving average. RBA at 4.85% vs SNB 0.00% maintains a +485bp nominal carry advantage for AUD, yet acute risk aversion (VIX 28.3, elevated volatility) has completely overwhelmed carry returns. Positioning data shows AUD levered funds net long +26,143 (pctl 19, z -0.86), while retail sentiment runs 88% long AUD/CHF, establishing an extreme retail accumulation fading institutional momentum. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF, dominated by CHF safe-haven flows overriding carry advantage during elevated cross-asset volatility. Catalyst: RBA Bulletin at 01:30 UTC. Risk: VIX retraces below 20, restoring carry appetite and triggering a short-squeeze in AUD cross pairs.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.22, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 158.82/158.18/158.93 following a breakout above 158.92. Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% provides a +275bp carry buffer (OIS SOFR 3.94% vs TONA 1.23% at +271bp), maintaining structural upside support. However, FX options show a strong put skew with 25d RR at -1.82 (Saxo, 1M tenor), reflecting institutional demand for downside protection as spot sits near the 160.00 threshold that previously triggered verbal intervention warnings. JPY COT LF net short stands at -29,545 (pctl 85, z +1.12), indicating crowded speculative short positioning vulnerable to sudden policy headlines. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported above moving average cluster while VIX remains below acute panic levels. Catalyst: Japan Tokyo Core CPI at 23:30 UTC (forecast 2.8%). Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 triggers official intervention or hawkish BoJ Tamura speech at 01:00 UTC.

signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3111, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3269/1.3280/1.3393 in a counter-trend pullback inside a larger downtrend. BoE Governor Bailey explicitly stated it is more likely than not that interest rates will need to rise further if energy prices remain elevated, contrasting with market pricing. BoE 4.00% vs Fed 4.00% provides a 0bp policy rate differential, while OIS SONIA 3.98% vs SOFR 3.94% gives GBP a slight +4bp carry edge. COT leveraged funds hold net long +23,730 (long% 60.4%), but experienced a sharp WoW reduction of -11,856 contracts, indicating speculative long unwinding into technical resistance. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD, counter-trend rally capped by overhead 20-day moving average cluster. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde Speech at 09:00 UTC and US Goods Trade Balance at 13:30 UTC. Risk: US 5Y yields extend recent 5-day decline (-21bp nominal, inflation-compensation-led), undermining USD support.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT-OIS Divergence + Retail Extreme
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5486, trapped below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5550/0.5613/0.5790 within a established downtrend. OIS rates price a hawkish market bias for RBNZ, yet leveraged funds remain net short -23,862 contracts (long% 25.3%, pctl 23), creating an active COT vs policy bias divergence. This institutional short positioning is heavily contrasted by Retail sentiment data retail sentiment showing an extreme 91% long build, establishing a textbook contrarian setup where retail is fading the primary trend. Fed 4.00% vs RBNZ 2.75% maintains a +125bp carry advantage for USD, while NZD Economic Surprise Index stands at -15.4 (strong negative bias), validating fundamental weakness. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, macro divergence and negative data surprises favor continued downside toward major support. Catalyst: US GDP 2nd estimate revision flow and US Initial Jobless Claims impact. Risk: Unexpected RBNZ hawkish shift forcing an institutional short-squeeze above 0.5550.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Extreme Positioning Stretch vs Model Value
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0973, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.1085/1.1200/1.1491 in a clear downtrend. CFTC positioning shows EUR leveraged funds short -105,891 contracts, reaching a pctl of 2 and z-score of -1.68, marking the extreme lower boundary of its 52-week range. Concurrently, the BEER fair value model flags EUR/USD as cheap at z = -2.47σ (spot 1.0973 vs fair value 1.1132). Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% maintains a +135bp carry advantage for USD (+150bp on OIS SOFR vs €STR basis), supporting structural downside despite oversold technical conditions. Trade bias: Neutral/range EUR/USD, downside momentum constrained by historical positioning floor and fair value misvaluation. Catalyst: Germany Unemployment Change at 08:55 UTC and Euro Area ESI at 10:00 UTC. Risk: US 2Y/10Y yield curve flattener accelerates, driving fresh USD buying through 1.0900.
